program.source: export function evaluate({ inputs, time, seed, state }) { const launchSpeed = inputs.launchSpeed; const gravity = 9.8; const t = time; const height = launchSpeed * t - 0.5 * gravity * t * t; const velocity = launchSpeed - gravity * t; const apexTime = launchSpeed / gravity; const apexHeight = (launchSpeed * launchSpeed) / (2 * gravity); const ballY = 320 - height * 40; const ballX = 320; const vValue = Math.abs(velocity); const vDir = velocity >= 0 ? "up" : "down"; const motionText = velocity > 0.1 ? "Moving up" : (velocity < -0.1 ? "Moving down" : "Still for an instant"); const calloutLines = [motionText, "Gravity pulls down"]; const lane = sdk.panel({ x: 40, y: 40, w: 560, h: 360, title: "Vertical Motion", state: motionText }); const axis = sdk.axis("axis.y", { x: 120, y: 340, length: 280, orientation: "y", min: 0, max: 2.5, ticks: [0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5], label: "Height", unit: "m" }); const guide = sdk.groundMark("mark.launch", 320, 340, 60, "Launch"); const ball = sdk.circle("ball.toss", ballX, ballY, 28, { role: "output" }); const vVec = sdk.vector("vec.v", { x: ballX + 20, y: ballY }, { value: vValue, direction: vDir }, { scale: 12, minLength: 0, label: "v" }); const aVec = sdk.vector("vec.a", { x: ballX - 20, y: ballY }, { value: gravity, direction: "down" }, { scale: 6, minLength: 16, label: "a" }); const callout = sdk.callout(ballX + 45, ballY - 20, calloutLines, { id: "callout.toss" }); const objects = [lane, axis, guide, ball, ...vVec, ...aVec, callout]; const motionStateVal = velocity > 0.1 ? "Moving up" : (velocity < -0.1 ? "Moving down" : "Still for an instant"); const gravityStateVal = "Pulling down"; return { frame: { width: 640, height: 420, objects: objects, readouts: [{ id: "motionState", value: motionStateVal }, { id: "gravityState", value: gravityStateVal }] }, quantities: { launchSpeed: launchSpeed, gravity: gravity, apexTime: apexTime, apexHeight: apexHeight, velocity: velocity, height: height } }; }

manifest.title: The ball stops rising. Gravity doesn’t stop.
manifest.summary: Gravity slows the ball on the way up and speeds it up on the way down. At the top, the ball is still for an instant while gravity still pulls downward.
manifest.description: A vertical height scale shows a tossed ball rising, pausing briefly at the apex, and falling back down. A blue velocity vector changes size and direction, while a dashed gravity vector remains constantly downward.
manifest.instructions: Change launch speed, then press Play. At the top, playback pauses so you can inspect the arrows. Press Play again to watch the ball fall, or drag the timeline to inspect any moment.
